title: Fluorescent pulse-chase labeling to monitor long-term mitochondrial degradation in primary hippocampal neurons
protocol: Euthanize an E18 timed-pregnant rat using an institution-approved protocol.
Spray the ventral area of the female rat with 70% ethanol.
Make a transverse incision between the dermal layer and abdominal fascia to expose the abdominal fascia.
Separate the layers and cut to expose the abdominal fascia.
Incise to open the abdominal cavity to expose the uterus.
Remove the uterus containing the prenatal pups.
Perform a lateral cut to remove the head of the rat.
Make an incision to the mid-sagittal plane of the skull to expose the brain.
Cut to separate the brain stem from the rest of the brain, leaving intact hemispheres.
Incise along the midline to divide the brain into right and left hemispheres.
Make an incision to open the abdomen using a fresh pair of scissors and forceps.
Cut to expose the abdominal cavity using a fresh pair of scissors and forceps.
Remove the uterus using a fresh pair of scissors and forceps.
Place the uterus in a 15 cm dish containing ice-cold HBSS.
Remove the embryos from the uterus.
Place the embryos into a 10 cm dish that contains ice-cold HBSS.
Separate and place the heads into a new 10 cm dish that has ice-cold HBSS.
Keep the plate on ice.
Place cold HBSS into the lid of a 10 cm dish.
Add the embryo heads to the lid containing cold HBSS.
Make an incision into the mid-sagittal plane of the head from posterior to anterior using vannas scissors.
Peel back the cranium.
Gently scoop under the brain in an anterior to posterior direction using a closed pair of vannas scissors to remove it from the skull.
Cut the brain stem to separate the brain.
Make a sagittal cut to separate the right and left hemispheres.
Remove the meninges from the brain’s surface using two fine-pointed forceps, starting from the exterior and working towards the interior.
With the interior hemisphere facing up, remove the hippocampus using vannas scissors.
Transfer the hippocampi to a 15 mL conical tube containing ice-cold HBSS using a P1000 pipette.
Remove HBSS from the 15 mL conical with a serological pipet.
Add 4.5 mL of warm HBSS and 0.5 mL of 2.5% trypsin to the conical tube.
Invert the conical once and incubate in a 37°C water bath for 10 min.
Stop digestion by removing the trypsin solution using a 10 mL serological pipet.
Add 10 mL of warmed AM, allow hippocampi to settle (approximately 30 s), and remove media using a 10 mL serological pipet.
Repeat step 18 two more times.
Add 1 mL of AM and triturate tissue with a fire-polished Pasteur pipette.
Dilute 10 μL of cell suspension with 10 μL of 0.4% Trypan Blue Stain.
Determine the cell viability and count using an automated counter.
Plate 1.25 × 10^5 cells onto the pre-coated/washed glass surface of 35 mm MatTek dishes containing warmed AM.
Add dropwise, covering the entire glass surface.
Keep cultures at 5% CO2 and 37°C for ∼2–5 h to provide adequate time for cells to settle and attach to the glass surface.
Ensure cells have adhered through visual inspection using a light microscope.
Upon confirmation, replace media with MM and maintain cultures at 37°C and 5% CO2.
The day after plating, or 1 day in vitro (DIV), add 1 μM AraC to cultures to prevent the proliferation of non-neuronal cells.
Dilute AraC in a small amount of MM (∼200 μL) and add it dropwise to the dish.
Gently mix to ensure there is an even distribution of AraC.
Every 3–4 days, replace ¼ of culture media with equilibrated MM.
Check the quality of neuron cultures at 6 DIV for viability before transfection.
Remove and save media from each imaging dish for later use.
Replace saved dishes with fresh equilibrated MM.
Prepare two separate mixtures in sterile microcentrifuge tubes for each transfection.
Incubate prepared mixtures at room temperature (20°C–22°C) for 5 min.
Add Tube 2 to Tube 1, gently mix by pipetting.
Incubate the mixture at 20°C–22°C for 20 min.
Add transfection complexes dropwise to neuron cultures.
Incubate the cultures at 37°C in 5% CO2 for 45 min.
During incubation, add equal parts of saved media from step 28 with fresh MM and equilibrate at 37°C in 5% CO2.
After 45 min, replace the neurons’ media with conditioned media.
Transiently transfect cells approximately 18 hours before pulse-chase labeling.
Remove media from each imaging dish and reserve for later use.
Save the removed media separately in sterile microcentrifuge tubes.
Incubate cells with mitochondrial-damaging conditions using AOF MM for 6 hours at 37°C in a Biosafety cabinet to induce mild oxidative stress.
Perform SNAP pulse-chase labeling during the final hour of the damaging incubation period.
Add ligand for 30 minutes, followed by two quick washes and a 30-minute washout period.
Label “Old” mitochondria with the first SNAP pulse.
Label “Young” mitochondria with the second SNAP pulse.
For SNAP-Cell Block labeling, add ligand for 120 minutes, followed by two quick washes and a 30-minute washout period.
Induce mitochondrial damage by adding 2 mL of AOF MM to each experimental plate.
For control condition, add 2 mL of regular MM to each control plate.
Place both plates in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 6 hours.
Add 100 nM of SNAP JF549cp and 100 nM of Halo JF646x ligands to each plate during the final hour of mitochondrial damage induction.
Thoroughly mix the plates and incubate for 30 minutes in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Wash plates twice with 2 mL of media.
Add 2 mL of media to each plate and place them back in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for a final 30-minute washout.
For treated plates, wash with AOF MM; for control plates, use regular MM.
Aspirate AOF MM from treated plates and add 2 mL of regular MM to both treated and control plates.
Add 1 μM of SNAP-Cell Block to each plate and thoroughly mix.
Incubate the plates in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 120 minutes.
Wash plates twice with 2 mL of media.
Add 2 mL of media to each plate and place them back in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for a final 30-minute washout.
Add conditioned media from step 34 back to imaging dishes and place them in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for approximately 16 hours.
Add 1 μM of SNAP-Cell 430 ligand.
Incubate for 30 min in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Wash plates twice with 2 mL of MM.
Add 2 mL of MM and place the dishes back in the 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for a final 30-min washout.
Aspirate media and add 2 mL of MM.
Turn on the temperature and CO2 controller before imaging.
Allow conditions to stabilize for approximately 1 hour.
Use MM media with a microscope equipped with a 5% CO2 environmental chamber for imaging neurons.
If not using such a microscope, use Hibernate E Low Fluorescence by BrainBits supplemented with B27 for ambient CO2 maintenance.
Design appropriate configurations for quantitative live-cell imaging to ensure good signal-to-noise ratio and avoid pixel saturation, fluorophore crosstalk, and accidental FRET.
Set up laser-scanning confocal using a Leica STELLARIS 8 equipped with a 63×/1.40 oil objective and LAS X Software.
Configure experimental channel setup to image SNAP 430, EGFP, SNAP JF546cp, and Halo JF646x.
Set acquisition parameters for SNAP-Cell 430 with Excitation at 440 nm and Emission from 450–486 nm, and for SNAP JF549cp with Excitation at 549 nm and Emission from 559–637 nm.
Configure acquisition parameters for EGFP with Excitation at 489 nm and Emission from 499–543 nm, and for Halo JF646x with Excitation at 647 nm and Emission from 657–750 nm.
Acquire Z-stack images in "Sequential Scanning" mode.
Use “Sequential Scanning” mode in LAS X.
Determine fluorophore crosstalk using the built-in crosstalk function.
Narrow the detection window of SNAP-Cell 430 to avoid crosstalk with EGFP.
Acquire images at a format of 1024 × 1024 (0.103 μm/pixel; image size 105.10 μm × 105.10 μm).
Use a step size of 0.3 μm, averaging 35–50 steps per image.
Perform bidirectional scanning with a scan speed of 600 Hz and a zoom factor of 1.75.
Set the line average to 2.
Adjust pinhole size to 1 AU.
Use the Over/Under look-up table to avoid pixel saturation throughout all Z-planes and for all channels.
Deconvolve images using LIGHTENING Process with an adaptive strategy, refractive index of 1.33, and water as mounting medium.
Set all channels to use 20 iterations, optimization of 1, regularization parameter of 0.05, and “Very High” smoothing.
Set contrast enhancement and cut-off to “Auto.”
Save image files for subsequent analysis.
Correct pixel misalignment during post-processing before analysis.
Use the “Rectangle” function to draw a box around a clear, well-defined event.
Create an overlay specific to the Z-stack slice for analysis.
Mark events that are OPTN-positive “Old” Mito-SNAP only; exclude events dual labeled with “Young” and “Old” Mito-SNAP.
Adjust brightness using the “Brightness & Contrast Tool.”
Toggle between channels using the “Channels Tool” to identify events.
View multiple Z-planes around the OPTN ring for confirmation.
Save each image file after visualizing all events in the cell.
Determine whether OPTN events containing “Old” mitochondria are positive or negative for LAMP1.
Visualize “Old” Mito-SNAP (SNAP JF549cp), Halo-OPTN (Halo JF646x), and LAMP1-EGFP channels using the “Channels Tool.”
Locate OPTN ring events using the boxes created in step 47.
Score OPTN-positive “Old” mitochondria for the presence or absence of LAMP1-EGFP.
Include clear, well-defined LAMP1 rings that colocalize with Halo-OPTN as LAMP1-positive events.
Exclude events without LAMP1-EGFP fluorescence signal or lacking colocalization of LAMP1-EGFP with Halo-OPTN around damaged mitochondria as LAMP1-negative.
Quantify the ratio of LAMP1-positive to total OPTN-positive “Old” mitochondria.
Divide the number of LAMP1-negative events by the total number of OPTN-positive “Old” mitochondria.
Generate representative line scans for OPTN-positive “Old” mitochondria events.
Draw a line (width = 1) through the Halo-OPTN ring using the “Line” function, avoiding high-fluorescence artifacts and saturated pixels.
Use “Plot Profile” and “List” to obtain fluorescence intensity values for each channel from the drawn line.
Draw a box in multiple representative areas using the “Rectangle” function.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of the image background using “Measure” in the “Analyze” tab.
Calculate the average background intensity for each channel.
Correct the fluorescence signal by subtracting the average background intensity from the measured values.
Normalize the intensity values for each channel by dividing each value by the overall highest intensity value for that channel.
Set the highest value to 1 and additional values to less than one.
Present data as bar graphs, scatter plots, or pie charts with representative images.
